## Argument

### 0. Conventions and inputs

All bases are locally Noetherian of characteristic zero. We use the packet CE convention W_5 = (O_{P(E^vee)}(2) tensor gamma^*O_{P^1}(-5))|_C, compatible with deg(W_f|_C)=4g+12-4f (sign constraint respected). Source-backed inputs used directly: SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 (obstruction decomposition and degree formula 4f+n-2g-14); packet adjudicated findings FND-0005, FND-0064, FND-0096, FND-0097, FND-0099; working-context established facts (degree table deg W_5=16, deg W_4=20, deg L=6, chi(L)=1; R^1p_*L_univ=0 and base change for Phi; kernel/cokernel of Phi at e; intrinsic derivative = Serre pairing isomorphism; degree-zero section criterion; Fitting ideals commute with arbitrary scalar extension; base-line twists leave Fitting ideals unchanged; reduced-support locus open and not closed; stack-level S_6-torsor). No blocked route is used; no finite computation carries universal weight.

### 1. Filtered CE reduction to the f=5 summand (no global splitting)

Balancedness supplies only the relative Harder-Narasimhan filtration 0 -> L_5 -> F -> L_4 -> 0; dualizing and twisting gives the canonical filtration 0 -> W_4 -> W -> W_5 -> 0 with deg W_4=20, deg W_5=16 (FND-0097; the global splitting constraint is respected: the extension class in Ext^1(L_4,L_5) subset H^1(B, gamma'_*O(1)) is not assumed zero). Since Gamma is finite over B, restriction to Gamma is exact. Exactness of pi_* on 0 -> W_4 -> W -> W_5 -> 0 requires R^1 pi_* W_4=0, which holds because deg W_4=20 > 2g-2=10 (FND-0099). The evaluation of W_4 at Gamma is surjective: fibrewise H^1(W_4(-Gamma))=0 because deg W_4(-Gamma)=14>10; cohomology-and-base-change plus Nakayama descend this to coker(phi_4)=0 as a sheaf (FND-0099). The snake lemma then gives coker(phi) ~= coker(phi_5), hence Fit_0(coker phi)=Fit_0(coker phi_5). This proves clause (1).

### 2. The SRC-0004 obstruction space is the evaluation cokernel (answering FND-0061)

From 0 -> W_5(-Gamma) -> W_5 -> W_5|_Gamma -> 0, coker(phi_5) ~= R^1 pi_* W_5(-Gamma) fibrewise. Serre duality gives H^1(W_5(-Gamma)) ~= H^0(omega_C tensor W_5^vee(Gamma))^vee. Thus the SRC-0004 groups H^0(omega_C tensor W_f^vee(Gamma)) are exactly the Serre duals of the CE evaluation cokernels, so the degree-zero analysis of those groups is an analysis of the CE evaluation map itself. At (6,6): deg(omega tensor W_4^vee(Gamma))=-4 gives H^0=0 identically (FND-0062), and deg(omega tensor W_5^vee(Gamma))=0 gives nonvanishing iff O_C(Gamma) ~= W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1}=L (FND-0063).

### 3. The universal determinantal identity Fit_0(coker Phi)=I_e

Let P=Pic^0(C/B), e:B->P the identity section, L_univ=omega_{C_P/P}(Gamma_P) tensor Poin^{-1} of relative degree 16>10. Then R^1p_*L_univ=0, E:=p_*L_univ has rank 11, F:=p_*(L_univ|_{Gamma_P}) has rank 6, and Phi:E->F commutes with arbitrary base change (established fact). Put J:=Fit_0(coker Phi), the ideal of 6x6 minors.

**3a. J subset I_e (Fitting base-change computation).** Base-change to e(B): e^*J = Fit_0(coker(e^*Phi)). The family exact sequence 0 -> omega -> omega(Gamma) -> omega(Gamma)|_Gamma -> 0 with R^1pi_*omega(Gamma)=0 (degree 16>10) identifies coker(e^*Phi) ~= R^1 pi_* omega, a line bundle on B, and im(e^*Phi)=ker(F -> R^1 pi_* omega) is a rank-5 subbundle. Locally splitting F = im + (line quotient), the matrix of e^*Phi has an identically zero row, so every 6x6 minor is zero as a function (not merely fibrewise): Fit_0(coker(e^*Phi))=0. Hence e^*J=0, i.e. J subset I_e. This is the sanctioned Fitting computation, not a radical/support argument.

**3b. Support.** For a point (C_b, N) of P with N in Pic^0(C_b), evaluation fails iff h^1(omega tensor N^{-1})>0, i.e. (Serre duality) h^0(N)>0, i.e. N ~= O by the degree-zero section criterion. Thus V(J)=e(B) set-theoretically.

**3c. I_e subset J (first-order minors plus explicit Nakayama).** Near e(b), trivialize E,F and put Phi(e(b)) in rank-5 normal form. The maximal-minor ideal is generated near e(b) by the six Schur-complement entries D-CA^{-1}B; their linear terms are the matrix coefficients of the intrinsic derivative delta: T_e P -> Hom(ker Phi_e, coker Phi_e). At e, ker Phi_e=H^0(omega) (dim 6), coker Phi_e=H^1(omega) (dim 1), and delta is cup product, identified by Serre duality with the perfect pairing H^1(O) x H^0(omega) -> H^1(omega); hence delta is an isomorphism of 6-dimensional spaces (established fact). Therefore the image of J spans (I_e/I_e^2) tensor k(b) for every b. Since I_e/(J+I_e^2) is a finitely generated O_B-module, Nakayama over A/I_e ~= O_B (the generation check required by the tangent-map constraint) gives I_e = J + I_e^2. Then I_e/J = I_e (I_e/J) with I_e inside the Jacobson radical of the local ring along e(B), so Nakayama over A gives I_e=J near e(B); away from e(B) both ideals are unit by 3b. Hence Fit_0(coker Phi)=I_e. This proves clause (2). (The determinantal expectation is attained here: rank <=5 for 11->6 has expected codimension (11-5)(6-5)=6=dim P/B; the expected-vs-actual codimension-4 constraint concerns the family image in M_{6,6} and is not invoked.)

### 4. Pullback to the balanced family: Z_ev = a^{-1}(e(B)) scheme-theoretically

Let a:B->P classify N_0 := omega_{C/B}(Gamma) tensor W_5^{-1} = O_C(Gamma) tensor L^{-1} in Pic^0. Then a^*L_univ ~= omega(Gamma) tensor N_0^{-1} ~= W_5, up to a line bundle pulled back from B; such twists leave Fitting/maximal-minor ideals unchanged (established fact). With R^1p_*L_univ=0, phi_5 is the underived pullback a^*Phi even when a is not flat (established fact). Fitting ideals commute with arbitrary scalar extension, so Fit_0(coker phi_5) = a^*J = a^*I_e, the ideal of the fibre product a^{-1}(e(B)). Hence Z_ev = a^{-1}(e(B)) as closed substacks. On geometric fibres this reads: Gamma in Z_ev iff O_C(Gamma) ~= L, and (Z_ev)_red is the reduced Abel-Jacobi incidence (consistent with, but stronger than, the geometric-point equality). This proves clause (3).

### 5. Stack descent

The construction so far is over scheme bases. For the universal ordered configuration stack, take a smooth scheme atlas U -> B^bal. Representability and smooth-locality of Pic^0, smooth-locality of Poincare pullbacks, base-change compatibility of pi_* under R^1=0, and Fitting-ideal formation are all smooth-local on the base; equality of the two quasi-coherent ideals holds over U by Step 4 and descends fpqc/smooth-locally. This supplies the atlas/descent remark required before any stack-level universal clause.

### 6. Source-backed corollary clauses (clause 4)

(a) Working-context established fact (mechanical, via relative duality O_{P(E^vee)}(1)|_C = omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2)): W_5 ~= omega_C^{tensor 2}(-D), so L ~= omega_C(-D) and the failure condition is Gamma in |omega_C(-D)|, equivalently D+Gamma canonical. FND-0105 localizes this to the CE relative-canonical normalization, with the residual twist forced trivial by degree; it is used only for this corollary clause, not for clauses (1)-(3).

(b) chi(L)=deg(L)-g+1=1 gives h^0(L)=1+h^1(L)>=1 on every smooth genus-6 geometric fibre, so the full Abel-Jacobi fibre in Sym^6 is nonempty (FND-0005, corroborated). Per FND-0083 this does NOT establish nonemptiness of the reduced-support open or of the ordered Conf_6 incidence on every fibre; that is left open (GAP-Z-RED).

(c) Conf_6 -> reduced-support open is a finite etale S_6-torsor on the stack of pairwise-distinct sections (FND-0064); the torsor fails on coarse moduli and is not asserted there (FND-0075). The reduced-support open is open and not closed; it is never called closed.

### 7. Exclusions and handoffs

Not claimed: monomorphism of the balanced model into M_{6,6} (FND-0098: equivalent to recovering gamma from L; the forgetful map is generically 5-to-1 and full-faithfulness over automorphism groups is not supplied); image/closure/components/dimensions/stabilizers in M_{6,6} (FND-0058, FND-0060, FND-0069, FND-0086; handed to C66-GEO-H0/C66-GEO-COMP); unbalanced tetragonal failure (FND-0091); constancy of h^0(L)=3 or pure dimension 17/codimension 4; identification of |L| with Proj(pi_*L) (FND-0047); any Tate, Gysin, localization, or exact-target statement (FND-0050, FND-0052, FND-0054, FND-0055).

### 8. Failed routes addressed

- Support-only ideal inclusion V(J)=e(S) => J subset I_e: replaced by the Fitting base-change computation Fit_0(coker(e^*Phi))=0 (Step 3a).
- Tangent-isomorphism-only generation of I_e/I_e^2: explicit Nakayama generation check over A/I_e included (Step 3c).
- Scheme-to-stack transfer without descent: smooth-atlas descent remark supplied (Step 5).
- Global splitting from fibrewise balancedness: filtered CE reduction used instead (Step 1, FND-0097/FND-0099).
- Scheme-theoretic equality from geometric points: Fitting/determinantal comparison supplied (Step 4, answering FND-0046).
- chi(L)=1 => ordered reduced nonemptiness: not walked; only Sym^6-fibre nonemptiness claimed (FND-0083).
- Reduced-support open called closed: not walked; stated open and not closed.
- Coarse-moduli S_6-torsor: not walked; stack-level only (FND-0064/FND-0075).

No blocked route (vcd-only-vanishing, undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex, point-count-without-degree-parity-separation, forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown) is used, and no new_inputs are declared.

gap_markers.clause_excluded: image/closure of Z_ev in M_{6,6}; components, dimensions, stabilizers, codimension
gap_markers.description: The theorem identifies Z_ev over the balanced tetragonal base only. Pushing to M_{6,6} forgets gamma; the forgetful map is generically 5-to-1 (five g^1_4's on a general genus-6 curve), and a monomorphism is equivalent to recovering the pencil from L with a stack-level full-faithfulness argument (FND-0098). Pure dimension 17/codimension 4 additionally needs constancy of h^0(L)=3 (FND-0058), stack-vs-coarse stabilizer analysis (FND-0060), and exclusion of larger special components (FND-0069, FND-0086). Handed to C66-GEO-H0/C66-GEO-COMP.

Unbalanced splitting types are not constructed (FND-0091: a theorem asserting the full CE failure locus in M_{6,6} is the balanced model while leaving unbalanced failure unconstructed is self-refuting). The present theorem is scoped to the balanced locus only.

summary: C66-GEO-Z construction step: the balanced CE evaluation-failure locus at (6,6) is identified scheme-theoretically, not merely on geometric points. The filtered CE reduction (FND-0097/FND-0099, splitting-free) collapses the obstruction to the f=5 evaluation phi_5. The universal evaluation Phi of omega(Gamma) tensor Poin^{-1} over the relative Picard scheme has determinantal/Fitting ideal exactly the ideal I_e of the identity section: inclusion J subset I_e is the Fitting base-change computation Fit_0(coker(e^*Phi))=0 (coker(e^*Phi) ~= R^1 pi_* omega is a line bundle, so all maximal minors vanish identically, even over nonreduced bases); the support is e(B) by the degree-zero criterion; and I_e subset J follows because the intrinsic derivative H^1(O) -> Hom(H^0(omega),H^1(omega)) is the Serre-pairing isomorphism, so first-order minors span I_e/I_e^2 fibrewise, with the generation concluded by an explicit Nakayama argument over A/I_e. Pulling back along the Abel-Jacobi map a (Fitting ideals commute with arbitrary scalar extension; base-line twists are inert) gives Z_ev = a^{-1}(e(B)) scheme-theoretically, descending to the ordered configuration stack by a smooth-atlas remark. This supplies the Fitting comparison demanded by FND-0046 and the obstruction-space linkage demanded by FND-0061. Remaining: image/closure/components/stabilizers in M_{6,6} (C66-GEO-COMP), h^0 stratification (C66-GEO-H0), unbalanced failure, reduced-support nonemptiness. theorem_statement: Theorem (scheme-theoretic identification of the balanced CE evaluation-failure locus at (g,n)=(6,6)). Work over locally Noetherian characteristic-zero bases, with the packet CE convention W_5 := (O_{P(E^vee)}(2) tensor gamma^*O_{P^1}(-5))|_C (the f_2=5 summand of (O(2) tensor gamma^*F^vee)|_C, not the O_{P^1}(5) summand of F). Let (pi:C->B, gamma) be a balanced tetragonal family of smooth genus-6 curves, let Gamma be a relative ordered Cartier divisor of degree 6 (a point of the ordered pairwise-distinct configuration stack), let 0 -> W_4 -> W -> W_5 -> 0 be the canonical filtered CE bundle (deg W_4=20, deg W_5=16), let phi: pi_*W -> pi_*(W|_Gamma) be the CE evaluation, and let Z_ev := V(Fit_0(coker phi)). Put L := W_5 tensor omega_{C/B}^{-1} (deg L=6) and let a: B -> Pic^0(C/B) classify O_C(Gamma) tensor L^{-1}. Then: (1) Fit_0(coker phi) = Fit_0(coker phi_5), where phi_5 is the W_5-evaluation (filtered reduction; no global splitting of W is used). (2) For the universal evaluation Phi of L_univ := omega_{C_P/P}(Gamma_P) tensor Poin^{-1} over P := Pic^0(C/B), one has Fit_0(coker Phi) = I_e, the ideal sheaf of the identity section e:B->P. (3) Z_ev = a^{-1}(e(B)) as closed substacks of the ordered configuration stack; equivalently Fit_0(coker phi_5) = a^*I_e. In particular, on every geometric fibre the points of Z_ev are exactly the ordered reduced degree-6 divisors Gamma with O_C(Gamma) isomorphic to W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1}, and (Z_ev)_red equals the reduced Abel-Jacobi incidence. (4) Source-backed corollary clauses: on the balanced locus W_5 ~= omega_C^{tensor 2}(-D) for D a fibre of gamma, so the failure condition is Gamma in |omega_C(-D)|, equivalently D+Gamma canonical; and chi(L)=1 forces h^0(L)>=1, so the full Abel-Jacobi fibre in Sym^6 is nonempty on every smooth genus-6 geometric fibre (reduced-support ordered nonemptiness is NOT asserted). Exclusions: no monomorphism into M_{6,6}; no image/closure/component/dimension/stabilizer claim in M_{6,6}; no h^0 stratification; no unbalanced-tetragonal failure construction; no global splitting W=W_4+W_5 over the base; no identification of the relative linear system with Proj(pi_*L); no closedness claim for the reduced-support open; no coarse-moduli torsor claim; no statement about the exact target group.
